conflicts.description: The Bellows Guild plans to break the noble witnessing monopoly by threatening to cut air to the Choir Vaults, while the Censer houses prepare to throttle guild allotments first.
conflicts.name: The Tithe Dispute

conflicts.description: The Silent Wardens conceal that the cathedral's hymn-sustained seals are failing. The Guild and the Censer each suspect the other of sabotage, and revealing the truth could trigger panic or a deadly power grab.
conflicts.name: The Secret of the Cracks

description: Far below the lightless surface of the ocean, at the bottom of a trench older than any map, lies a colossal cathedral that sank in an age no one records. Its vaults now hold a living city, sealed against the crushing deep by saltglass windows and the old prayers carved into its stones. Merchants and nobles scheme in this mysterious, shadow-lit fantasy realm for adults. Wealth is counted in air, light, and the favor of the cathedral itself. The nobles claim descent from the original clergy and rule by liturgical right. The merchants control the bellows, the pearl-lamps, and the trade with surface wrecks, and they are growing impatient. Every contract is sworn before a drowned altar that remembers each lie. Beneath the court intrigue, the cathedral's foundations are shifting, and someone is hiding why.

factions.description: The noble houses that claim descent from the cathedral's clergy. They rule through liturgical law and hoard knowledge of the old rites.
factions.name: House of the Censer

factions.description: A merchant consortium that controls air, light, and salvage trade. They want a seat at the altar and an end to noble tithes.
factions.name: The Bellows Guild

factions.description: A secretive order of oath-witnesses who tend the altar and never speak outside it. They know the cathedral is failing and tell no one.
factions.name: The Silent Wardens

history.description: The cathedral sank into the trench with its congregation inside, and the first prayers sealed the windows.
Survivors built the first air-bellows in the side aisles, founding the merchant trade.
The noble houses decreed the witnessing tithe, cementing their authority over commerce.
The Silent Wardens swore a vow of silence after a perjured treaty drowned an entire noble line at the altar.
A hairline fracture appeared in a saltglass window above the Bellows Quarter, and the Wardens quietly sealed the record of it.

locations.description: The soaring upper galleries of the cathedral, now home to noble houses. Pipes of the sunken organ still hum when pressure shifts, and nobles read the tones as omens.
locations.name: The Choir Vaults

locations.description: A crowded warren in the cathedral's side aisles. Merchants run the great air-bellows and pearl-lamp markets here. Whoever controls the air-lines controls the city.
locations.name: The Bellows Quarter

locations.description: The flooded sanctum at the cathedral's heart. Oaths sworn over its black water are binding, and perjurers are said to be taken by the altar's cold current.
locations.name: The Drowned Altar

name: The Drowned Nave

rules.statement: Breathable air is rationed through the bellows lines, and debts are legally enforceable by throttling a debtor's allotment.
An oath sworn over the drowned altar binds the swearer, and breaking it causes the water to rise against them.
Saltglass windows hold back the trench's pressure only while the cathedral's hymns are sung or played within hearing of them.
No natural light reaches the city, so pearl-lamps are the only reliable illumination and a vital commodity.
By cathedral law, every merchant contract must be witnessed by a noble house, which takes a tithe.
